name: v6-arm-b-mining
recorded: 2026-10-12, before any candidate row was scored, selected or read for yield. The only reads behind this record: the v5 seed-1 checkpoint's sha256 (campaign/span-refit-mac-preregistered.json), the committed source of choice_rule_abstentions at d930579, the sha256 of the existing pool and corpus files named below, and Fable's rulings. No scorer output of any candidate exists.
status: pre-registration of the mining rule, driver and 200-row probe. The full scan is wave 3 and is not started by this record. Mac rows are quick-labelled where they cannot promote (CLAUDE.md rule 8); the mined rows themselves are training data for the v6 run, whose own pre-registration (campaign/v6-preregistered.json) is the promotion instrument.
design_by: Fable v6 data-design ruling R4 and R8 (AUDIT/v6-rulings-2026-10-08/fable-v6-data-design-ruling.md); human rulings 2026-10-08 (Arm B mining runs on the Mac under the lock; synthetic and own-repo data only); Fable board-sweep ruling 2026-10-12 section 3 lane 6.
question: Which in-distribution rows does v5 seed 1 abstain on although their constructed gold is not noul? Arm B teaches when not to abstain: the binding half of ood_abstain is the in-distribution cap (v5 8.2%, cap 5%).

scorer.what: v5 seed 1's checkpoint, not the average: average_may_promote is false, and the average abstains least, so it would mine the fewest rows (R4).
scorer.path_through: tools/real_ft_run.py --score-checkpoint over a candidate shard set, with --verdicts-out; Mac/MPS under tools/mac_heavy.sh. qd-metal is refused: its batched decode is KNOWN RED on the GPU digest pin (9c563ed) and serves bf16.

selection_rule.function_sha256_of: the source text of that function (ast.get_source_segment) in tools/real_ft_run.py at commit d930579; the driver recomputes it from the committed blob and refuses to run on a mismatch
selection_rule.rule: a candidate row is KEPT iff the runtime's generic-route choice rule would abstain on it (the first pass's top row is noul, or the permuted pass's top row is noul, or the permuted pass's winner maps back to a different option) AND its constructed gold is not noul (expected_abstain is false). tools/arm_b_mine.py re-implements the rule over --verdicts-out lines and a parity test holds it to choice_rule_abstentions.
selection_rule.label: the row's constructed class, untouched.

candidates.rule: fresh rows, labelled by construction, never duplicates. Every corpus is pinned here by sha256 BEFORE the first row is scored; a corpus whose entry below has sha256 null is refused by the driver. Pinning a null is done by an amendment commit that records only the file's sha256 and row count, with no scorer output read.

corpora.name: commitpackft-composed-ts-v1

Row count amended 4000 -> 1250: compose's symmetric-roles rule needs one distinct needle file per mutated row, and the TypeScript-restricted v3 corpus has only 1,039 train files with a mutated rendering, so 1,250 is the maximum (1,270 and above are refused with 'only 1039 files have a mutated rendering'). superseded_pin.why: `--limit 12000` over the whole pool stops at the first 12,000 examples in pool order, so that corpus held python and go only. Superseded, not rewritten: no scoring had happened.

exclusion.exact_identity_dedupe: a candidate whose id, identity_key or content digest sha256(before NUL after) equals a key of any set below is dropped and counted by set; within-candidate duplicates are dropped and counted. A candidate whose repo is a held-out repository of the own-repos manifest, or whose path carries a held-out marker, is refused whole (CLAUDE.md rule 3). Duplicating v5 train rows is refused.

sets.name: v5-val-verdict-row-ids
sets.note: row_id values are `qdm:code.defect_class:<corpus id>`; compared by normalised key.

exclusion.leakage_scans: the containment scan against val, held-out and target texts (qd-prep containment, the v5 scan), the v2 split map (sha f5621909...) and the pipeline's v6 split-priority dedupe. The driver records each as ran (with its attestation sha256) or not_run; an absent scan is never recorded as clean. The driver records heldout_exact_keys and v6_split_priority_dedupe as not_run (no held-out key set is pinned; the pipeline runs the dedupe).

split_map.note: regenerated 2026-10-12 by tools/compose_split_map.py over the pinned pool; reproduces the v2 split map's sha256. The driver drops candidates whose repo is val or heldout in it, and refuses a repo it does not hold unless the corpus is flagged own_repos_train (own-swift-composed-v1 is selected from the own-repos manifest's train repositories).

exclusion.key_normalisation: ids are compared after stripping the mixture prefix `qdm:<family>:` (v5's verdict row ids carry it; corpus ids do not). Amended 2026-10-12 before any scoring: the unnormalised comparison matched 0 of 2,304 v5 val ids.

throughput.probe: the first 200 deduped candidate rows, in the corpus order the seed fixed, scored once as a heavy MPS job under tools/mac_heavy.sh. It measures rows_per_s. Its abstention count is recorded, gates nothing and is not read as a yield estimate.
throughput.formula: rows_scanned = min(20000, floor(rows_per_s x 36 x 3600)); the scan runs in lock chunks of at most 6 h; total wall cap 36 h.

caps.no_data: fewer than 300 kept rows reads `no_data`: v6 runs without them, and Arm B's reading is `not_run`. Nothing is promoted or padded to reach the floor.
caps.applied_pool: mined rows enter no pool until the caller families' rows exist and Arm B has rows or reads no_data (board-sweep ruling 2f(ii)); this record writes no applied pool.

reading_rule.arm_b: ood_abstain.in_distribution over code.defect_class: Wilson upper <= 5% on at least 2 of 3 seeds, with the OOD suite half >= v5's same seed on every seed.
reading_rule.needle: worst depth bucket >= 0.95 on every seed, with Swift and TS reported per language.
reading_rule.guards: val choice top-1 >= 0.8278 and span >= 0.9066 on every seed.

refuses: a pre-registration that is not committed or differs from HEAD
a corpus or scorer whose sha256 is null or differs from this record
any input path with a held-out marker, or an input file holding a caller record (rule 3)
a candidate that duplicates a v5 train or val key
a candidate from a held-out repository
driver.records: every count (offered, refused by reason, duplicates by set, kept, abstained) and the sha256 of every input and output, in the plan and report files it writes beside the rows.
driver.select: `select` takes --plan-dir and refuses verdicts whose row ids are not in the plan (the scorer ran over another shard set).

amendments: an amendment is a new commit that changes a null above to a sha256 and a row count, before any scoring; any other change after a candidate was scored is void.
